requirement:
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the test adequately checks `requirements.cli.refactor_skill.workflow`. It is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_moves_first_then_updates_evidence_with_habeas_refactor]`, and it is marked `{test}` for the subject.

**What the test does.** The requirement constrains the text and order of the `habeas-refactor` skill. The test calls `assert_in_order("habeas-refactor", …)`. That helper loads the whole skill (`SKILL.md` plus its references) with whitespace collapsed, using `bundled_skill`. `assert_text_in_order` then requires each phrase to appear after the previous one and panics with a message if one is missing. It is a real assertion, and it also enforces the order of the steps.

**Obligations mapped to phrases.** I read `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md` to confirm that the Workflow section contains each phrase.

| Obligation | Test phrase(s) | Skill step |
|---|---|---|
| Make the move with the agent's own edits, kept separate from other changes | "Make the move with your own edits", "Change nothing else in this step" | 1 |
| Run `habeas refactor --dry-run` with a mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name | "`habeas refactor --dry-run` with one `--map <old>=<new>` for every moved file or directory, node, and definition name" | 2 |
| Review the report, including records left unchanged and the rationale spans it lists | "Review the report", "lists the records it updates, with each code span in their rationales that still mentions an old path", "lists records a mapping affects that fail a check" | 3 |
| Run without `--dry-run` | "Run the same command without `--dry-run`" | 4 |
| Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale | "`habeas status`. Only the records the report left unchanged" | 5 |
| Commit the move and evidence update before changing behavior | "Commit the move, the rewritten references, and the `evidence/` changes together, before any change to behavior or text" | 6 |
| Then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill | "Next, reassess what remains stale with `habeas author --all`, following the habeas-evidence skill" | 7 |

The phrases appear in the same order as the requirement's sequence: move, dry run, review, real run, status, commit, then reassess.

**Cited requirements.** `requirements.refactor.dry_run`, `requirements.refactor.mappings`, and `requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched` are context only. I did not reassess their tests. The skill's own text applies them: the dry-run direction, a mapping for every file, node, and definition name, and review of the unchanged records and rationale spans. The test asserts all of that.

**Other tests.** `bundled_skill_workflows_end_by_naming_the_skill_for_the_next_task` also checks the final step, but I did not rely on it.

**Limits.** The check is phrase-based, so a paraphrase would fail it. That is stricter, not looser, and it is the practical way to test a prose requirement about skill text. I found no plausible skill wording that drops an obligation, such as skipping the dry run, omitting the status check, or committing after behavior changes, and still passes the test. I found no gap, and no `{fixme}` applies.

text: :::{req} refactor_skill.workflow
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
:::{req} dry_run
With `--dry-run`, `habeas refactor` MUST report every change it would make,
in the same form as {cite}`requirements.refactor.command`, and MUST write
nothing.
:::{req} mappings
Each `--map` MUST have one of these forms:
- a file or directory path, which maps that file, or every file under that
directory, to the same relative path under the new side;
- `<file>#<selector>`, which maps one outline node, and its outline
descendants, to the node at the new file and selector;
- a definition name, which maps that full name, and every full name beginning
with it followed by `.`, to the same suffix under the new name.
A mapping whose old side names a recorded definition, or a prefix of one
followed by `.`, MUST be a definition-name mapping.
:::{req} rationale.untouched
`habeas refactor` MUST NOT change rationale text other than the spans
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.names`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.paths`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.addresses` cover. For each changed
record, it MUST list the other code spans in the rationale that contain an old
side of a path or node mapping, so the user can review them.
